KSH’s 1H2027 profit rises 23% on gains from Singapore condo JVs
article:
KSH Holdings ’ earnings rose 23.3% y-o-y to $6.5 mil for the six months ended Sept 30 (1HFY2027). The increase came mainly from its Singapore residential joint ventures, which moved from losses into profit.

The group’s share of results from associates and joint ventures was a profit of $3.7 mil, compared with a loss of $1.8 mil a year earlier. KSH, which announced its results on Nov 13, credited higher sales and construction progress at its Singapore development projects. The property development segment added $3.2 mil to earnings, up from a $3.7 mil loss in 1HFY2026.

That gain offset weaker results from construction, KSH’s core business. Project revenue rose 22.8% to $75.0 mil on higher work progress, but construction costs rose faster, by $15.5 mil to $63.2 mil. Construction’s contribution to earnings fell to $4.9 mil from $7.2 mil. Group revenue rose 21.7% to $76.8 mil.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

KSH has stakes in four Singapore residential projects, all launched and under construction. Its biggest stake (49%) is in the freehold, 172-unit The Arcady at Boon Keng , where 69% of the units have been sold at an average of $2,607 psf, based on caveats lodged with URA Realis as at Nov 15.

KSH also holds a 20% stake in the 440-unit, 99-year leasehold Sora at Yuan Ching Road, which is 55% sold at an average of $2,243 psf. The freehold, 113-unit Bagnall Haus , in which KSH has a 12% stake, is 97% sold at an average of $2,504 psf.

KSH’s smallest stake (10%) is in The Collective at One Sophia , the 367-unit residential component of the One Sophia mixed-use development. The 99-year leasehold project is 26% sold at an average of $2,767 psf.

As at Sept 30, KSH’s share of revenue from units sold but not yet recognised was more than $148 mil. This will be booked as construction progresses.

The group also has stakes in three industrial joint ventures: Gate+ at Tukang Innovation Drive (10%), Tukang Innovation Drive Plot B (30%) and Thomson Gem at Upper Thomson Road (25%). The other two have not been launched yet.

KSH says sales at Gate+, launched in May and now under construction, have been satisfactory. About 46% of its 265 multiple-user factory units have been sold at an average of $605 psf, based on caveats lodged as at Nov 15. Gate+ has a 33-year lease from August 2025.

“Our property development joint venture projects in Singapore and China continue to make steady progress,” says Choo Chee Onn, executive chairman and managing director of KSH. “At the same time, our expansion into industrial properties adds another avenue for growth and further diversifies our property investments.”

In China, sales continued at KSH’s two projects in Singapore Sino Health City, Gaobeidian. Both phases of Zhong Xin Yue Lang are complete. Some 93% of the 812 units in Phase 1 have been sold, as have 37% of the 1,020 units launched in Phase 2.

At Zhong Xin Yue Shang, 98% of the 1,011 units in the completed Phase 1 have been sold. In Phase 2, 94% of the 204 completed units have been sold. A further 1,011 units have been launched, with 12% sold so far, and are slated for completion in FY2027.

Still, China weighed on earnings. Other operating expenses rose $1.8 mil to $4.2 mil, mainly because of a provision for land appreciation tax in China and a loss on the disposal of associates. Rental income from investment properties fell to $1.8 mil from $2.1 mil, owing to lower occupancy and exchange rate effects on rental income from China.

KSH’s construction order book stood at about $887 mil as at Sept 30. The group says this is expected to support its performance through FY2030.

Gearing stood at 0.32 times, with cash and fixed deposits of $142.5 mil. Net asset value per share was 50.89 cents.

title: CENTURION: More Beds, Strong Revenue Growth -- Maybank Remains Bullish
article:
Centurion Corporation’s expanding accommodation portfolio is delivering sharply higher revenue, with new beds and acquisitions driving a
41%
year-on-year increase to
S$95.2 million
in 3Q2026.

Nine-month revenue rose 35% to S$280.1 million, helped by the consolidation of Westlite Mandai, additional Singapore beds, Malaysia’s Harum Megah portfolio and EPIISOD Macquarie Park in Sydney.
Centurion continues to perform much of the management and operational work for Centurion Accommodation REIT (CAREIT), after transferring properties to the listed REIT in Sept 2025. Centurion earns management fees from properties it no longer wholly owns. It also benefits from distributions on its retained 38.25% REIT units.

CENTURION

Share price:
$1.21

Target:
$1.78

Maybank Research sees “clear revenue/earnings visibility” as the portfolio expands.

Analyst Eric Ong maintains his
BUY recommendation and S$1.78 target price
, implying 47% upside from the recent S$1.21 stock price.

New beds begin to contribute

•
Worker accommodation:
It remained the main revenue generator, bringing in S$219.6 million over nine months, up 35%.

Average financial occupancy in Singapore eased to 94% from 99%, reflecting the addition of 5,460 beds that are still filling up.
The new Westlite Mandai beds are fully committed, with tenancies expected to be fully in effect by early 2027.

Malaysia presents a different challenge.
Average occupancy fell to 73% from 83% as foreign-worker caps constrained recruitment.
Revenue nevertheless rose 31%, mainly because of the acquired Harum Megah portfolio.
Management reported a slight improvement in occupancy in 3Q and expects further progress.

y business segment

•
Student accommodation
: Revenue increased 32% to S$57.6 million, while average financial occupancy improved to 97% from 94%. Macquarie Park was a major growth contributor, although its occupancy is counted at 100% under a master lease.

Australia’s new key worker accommodation business also started contributing.
Concorde South Hedland operated at near-full occupancy, while October’s acquisition of Velocity Karratha expanded the portfolio to approximately 446 beds.
Both properties are expected to contribute in the fourth quarter.

Major additions include:

•  a 7,974-bed acquisition in Johor, scheduled to complete in April 2027, and
• 12,000 beds at Singapore’s Kranji Close and Lok Yang Way, expected to open in 3Q2028.

That provides visibility on expansion, although the Singapore developments’ first full year of operations would be 2029.

Chief executive Kong Chee Min said:

“Our focus now is on execution: delivering these projects on schedule and ramping up occupancy at the new beds we have added in Singapore.”

For the nearer term, management maintained its approximately S$190 million revenue guidance for the second half.
This implies 4Q revenue of around S$94.8 million, broadly matching 3Q.

What Maybank’s forecasts tell investors

Analyst Eric Ong wrote:

“We leave our FY26-28E estimates and TP of SGD1.78 (based on 1.1x FY27E P/B) unchanged for now. Maintain BUY.”

Thus, Maybank's bullish case rests not only on Centurion's expanding accommodation portfolio but also on the prospect of a higher market valuation.
Its S$1.78 target assumes the shares trade at 1.1 times FY2027 book value, compared with 0.75 times at S$1.21.
Maybank projects FY2026 core profit attributable to shareholders of
S$96.7 million, down 10.9%
, followed by S$102.5 million in FY2027 and S$109.2 million in FY2028.

title: Tata heir questions big bets as US$185 bil group feud deepens
article:
(Nov 15): Noel Tata, chairman of the trusts that control Tata Group, questioned whether some of the conglomerate’s biggest investments are being executed with enough discipline, deepening a dispute over capital allocation, control and a potential listing of its holding company.

The clash has widened as the group commits billions of dollars to semiconductors, aviation, electronics and electric-vehicle batteries, while the trusts that own 66% of Tata Sons Pvt resist a listing that would bring outside shareholders into the closely held parent. The dispute now reaches beyond succession and ownership to how a group generating about US$185 billion in annual revenue is funded, governed and run.

“The question is, do we have the discipline when we execute projects, and not the direction?” Tata said on Saturday at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi. “How will projects with a long gestation period succeed if we don’t have discipline?”

Much of the expansion has been pursued under Natarajan Chandrasekaran, the professional executive who has led Tata Sons since 2017. A confidential analysis prepared by Tata Trusts and reviewed by Bloomberg News estimated that semiconductors, electronics and aviation would require more than two trillion rupees in additional capital.

The governance dispute widened after Tata Sons’ board backed Chandrasekaran for another five-year term on Sept 17 despite Noel Tata’s opposition. A spokesperson for Tata Sons didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment on his remarks about execution, capital allocation and a possible listing, sent over the weekend.

Tata companies generated about US$185 billion in revenue in the year through March and own businesses ranging from Jaguar Land Rover to Tetley tea. Tata Trusts owns 66% of Tata Sons, and profits from group companies ultimately help fund philanthropy.

See also: ‘Anti-AI’ trade turns Indian equities into Asia’s bright spot

That ownership structure has also allowed Tata Sons to support businesses through periods of weak returns or heavy investment. Noel Tata has argued that a public listing, and the arrival of thousands of outside shareholders, could make that model harder to sustain.

“My worry is that listing, which is what some people are proposing, will change the Tata way,” he said. With 30,000 to 40,000 shareholders, “profit may take precedence over philanthropy.”

Pressure to go public intensified after the Reserve Bank of India classified Tata Sons as an upper-layer non-banking financial company, a designation that carries listing requirements. The Trusts have opposed that outcome and explored a restructuring aimed at keeping the parent private.

See also: Asia’s richest banker sees AI correction boosting flows to India

Noel Tata said the Trusts remain “100% behind” investments in projects of national importance, even as he called for greater discipline in how the group executes them and allocates capital.
